area: WAYS - the lane web, the straggler service, the sweeps, the joints, the track and connector, the crossings and bridges, and REACH
read: tests: hamletgen/test_pool_261.py, gate/test_lane_network.py, gate/test_crossings_and_cover.py, gate/test_cohort_lane_rules.py, soak/test_seed_43_kink.py, soak/test_polder_fall_0.py, gate/hamletgen/test_driver.py, hamletgen/test_driver.py, hamletgen/test_unreached_houses.py

architecture.summary: The web is ~40 passes, each with its own partial guard ('no worse than it was', 'least bad', 'keep the orphan'). No single pass can own a web-wide rule, and nothing after the passes re-asks them. The design keeps the passes as best-effort drawing and adds three things that together make every rule below a guarantee: (M1) ONE lane-law module holding every predicate the tests assert, read by placer and test alike; (M2) settle_the_web, the LAST pass of stage_web, a repair loop that only REMOVES material from non-tree lanes or DRAWS reserved access corridors, with a termination argument; (M3) the access-corridor tree reserved at seating, which replaces the driver's re-roll as the reach guarantee; plus (M4) two reorders so that nothing after stage_web rewrites a lane.

M1_lane_law.where: new module l7r/diagram/hamletgen/ways/law.py (a lift, not a re-derivation: each predicate is the body a test asserts today, moved to the engine and the test rewritten to import it)

predicates.bends_badly(pts): the tests' _kinks: a turn >= DOUBLE_BACK_DEG (140) or two turns >= 50 deg whose SUMMED path between them is <= 40 ft (replaces clearance._bends_badly, which tests one segment only - FR-003 mismatch named by R1 row 18)
predicates.hooked_ends(pts): last/first leg <= joints._HOOK_FT (12) turning >= _HOOK_DEG (90); asked of every lane including the connector (test_pool_261 asks all lanes, test_lane_network skips the connector - the stricter reading is taken)
predicates.folded_joints(lanes): joints.joints/oriented + turn >= 140 at an end-to-end joint
predicates.connector_hairpins(lanes): joints.hairpin_over_a_short_leg over every lane end at the connector's start
predicates.needle_joins(lanes): NEW: a lane end whose last leg meets another tread at < NEEDLE_DEG over > NEEDLE_FT (thresholds a map drawing convention, recorded at the constant with Mizuguchi's 16 deg / 35 ft as the motivating case)
predicates.doubled_tails(lanes): sweeps.along_tail at _DOUBLED_DEG against every other lane, no width exemption
predicates.crossing_faults(pts, streams, channels,: per brook: crossings < 2; each crossing within FORD_HALF (30 ft) of a recorded ford (ONE constant; the test's 45 ft slack existed only because round_the_brooks moved the course after the fords, which M4 removes); each crossing of a stream or drawn channel within FORD_SQUARE_TOL_DEG of square
predicates.deck_seats(pts, waters): for every crossing of every bridge_crossed_waters course: settlement/city/bridges.py:seat_deck(...)[2] is True - the same call bridges() makes
predicates.fouls_fabric(pts, width, steadings, pass: fabric._hits_a_steading at the lane's own width, or _crosses_fabric against other households' yards/gardens at _TOUCH_GAP; a door path is exempt only from its OWN steading
predicates.networks(lanes): len(set(geom._components(ways, _TOUCH_GAP))) - the ink-continuity reading both network tests use (JOIN_TOL 4 == _TOUCH_GAP)
predicates.dangling_ends(M): geom.end_serves over the other lanes MINUS those within _TOUCH_GAP of the lane's own far end (test_no_lane_end_is_served_only_by_the_way_it_left's segment set; strictly stronger than test_lane_network's, so one predicate serves both)
predicates.doorstep_ends(M): the test's count: free non-connector ends (no other way within 4 ft) whose nearest farmhouse is within 80 ft; > 2 per house is a violation
predicates.way_outs_crossing(M): departure_routes(M) with > 1 crossing of any brook
predicates.unreached_houses(M): the existing ways/checks.py predicate (served_network at LANE_JOIN_FT, WEB_REACH_FT) - unchanged, lifted in feature 166
predicates.field_unreached(M): brook map and no non-connector lane within 60 ft of worked ground (test_a_way_reaches_the_field's own computation)

M2_settle_the_web.where: l7r/diagram/hamletgen/ways/settle.py:settle_the_web(s, plan, tree) called as the last line of web.py:stage_web (after a_way_onto_the_bund)
M2_settle_the_web.loop: repeat until one full round changes nothing: (1) SQUARE: normalize every lane at every stream/drawn-channel crossing with checks.square_crossings (fixed: split a too-short segment at the crossing instead of skipping it, square EVERY crossing on a segment, not only the first); (2) SHAPE: for each non-tree lane violating bends_badly / hooked_ends / crossing_faults / deck_seats / fouls_fabric, cut the lane at the offending vertex or segment and keep only pieces that pass (a hairpin or kink: drop the shorter side; a hook: shorten by one vertex; a fabric foul, an off-ford, off-square-after-normalize or undeckable crossing: cut the segment out; even crossings: cut between them); (3) WAY OUTS: while way_outs_crossing is non-empty, drop the non-tree, non-connector lane piece carrying the offending route's crossing farthest from the connector; (4) REACH: for every house in unreached_houses, draw its reserved corridor chain (M3) up to its first contact with the served network; (5) NETWORK: drop every lane component not containing the connector (tree lanes are never in such a component - they are joined through the root); (6) ENDS: trim each non-tree lane whose end fails dangling_ends with _trim_to_service at the aligned predicate, drop it if it trims away; the same for doorstep_ends (trim the extra ends of non-tree lanes), doubled_tails (cut_at_tail), needle_joins (cut the needle leg back to the prior vertex), connector_hairpins (drop the short leg), folded_joints (drop the shorter of the two records' last legs), husks (drop); (7) FIELD: if field_unreached, draw the reserved field corridor (M3).
M2_settle_the_web.termination: steps 1-3 and 5-6 only remove material from NON-tree lanes (a sub-polyline of a lane passes every per-lane law the lane passed except hooked_ends, which is handled by removing further - so removal never creates a new shape violation it cannot finish), and total non-tree length strictly falls on every change; steps 4 and 7 only add tree edges, of which there are at most households + 2. So the loop ends, and it ends with every predicate of M1 empty. Tree edges pass every per-lane law by construction (they were admitted by the same predicates at seating, and their ground was held clear) and are never cut.
M2_settle_the_web.fr005: no step keeps a least-bad violating lane: a lane that cannot be repaired is dropped, and a house or the field it served is then served by its reserved corridor. The existing fallbacks that emitted violations are converted at their sites too (rows below), so settle is the guarantor, not the only line.
M2_settle_the_web.cost: each round runs departure_routes, served_network and _components once; measured bound expected 1-3 rounds on the pool (the pool maps pass every rule today, so settle changes nothing on them unless M3/M4 moved them). Index: the lane segments go in one PointGrid rebuilt per round (settlement/_geom/indexes.py), which every predicate asks.

M3_access_corridor_tree.why_this_and_not_the_18_attempts: future-work 2b records that every seat-time reach test failed for one reason: whether a way can reach a steading depends on FINAL fabric, and a test asked while fabric is still being laid either ignores the fabric (too permissive, attempts 7, 8, 13-line) or counts the neighbors' own yards, which every seat touches by construction (too strict, attempt 13-width). A RESERVED corridor removes the premise: once house N's corridor is reserved, no later part can be laid on it, so the fabric that exists when N is seated is the only fabric its corridor must clear - and it need only reach the nearest RESERVED strip (fabric-free by construction), not a neighbor's house through their yard. The way-drawing attempts (10-12) failed because on 5 of 8 stranded houses no walkable path existed once the cluster was finished; reservation makes one exist by construction. It is the 'packer must RESERVE ways' of 2b's own title.
M3_access_corridor_tree.root: at the start of stage_homesteads (after install_site_boundary), reserve the EXIT RAY: from the seat center along seat['out'] to the band bound plus TRACK_FABRIC_GAP + 8 (the line _cluster_gateway already leaves along), clipped at the first hard ground or brook. The connector starts at its outer end (M4b).
M3_access_corridor_tree.per_seat: in settlement/rolling/fit.py:_parts_fit (beside _house_unreachable), for the homestead geometry under test: door = the yard-facing wall point serve.py already computes (lift that expression to law.door_of(house, yard)); candidates = the straight run from the door to the foot on each of the k=6 nearest tree segments, plus the dog-leg through the yard's outer corner; each normalized (square at stream/channel crossings) and admitted only if: clear of every placed part at FOOTPATH_FABRIC_GAP + 1.5 ft half tread (the house's OWN yard excepted; its own garden, kura and shed not); clear of web hard ground at WEB_HARD_GAP; crossing the brook only at a ford, and only where the tree does not already cross that brook (one tree crossing per brook - what makes the way-out rule provable); not bends_badly after normalization; deck_seats at every crossing; and the chain to the root crosses each brook at most once. The first admitted candidate is the house's corridor; with none, the seat is refused and the next seat offered (the same refusal path _house_unreachable uses).
M3_access_corridor_tree.reserved_against: a new registry s.access_corridors (segments with half-width), a PointGrid of segments; asked by FOOTPRINT (not center-only like _near_corridor) by: _envelope_blocked/_parts_fit/_bundle_side_fits for every later homestead; stage_appurtenances (byres, sheds, wells, privies), stage_pond_stock, stage_burial through one predicate s.on_access_corridor(poly). Released after stage_web (the undrawn ones), so the woods, belt and bamboo are unchanged by the reservation.
M3_access_corridor_tree.field_corridor: the first front-row house whose door has a clear straight run to the bund (bund.run_on_target) reserves it as the tree's FIELD edge, admitted by the same predicates (a ditch crossing allowed, decked; the brook at a ford). Front-row seats keep being offered until one does; recorded in meta.field_corridor.
M3_access_corridor_tree.dispersed: no tree: unreached_houses and the field rule do not apply to a dispersed hamlet (the predicate's own form condition).

M4_reorders.a_round_the_brooks: move frame.round_the_brooks out of stage_crossings to the end of the water stages (after stage_sink, before stage_seat), and write the rounded course back to plan.brook / plan.sink_brook, so the fords (track.py:275), the corridors, the router and the decks all read ONE course. Today it reshapes the brook after the fords and the lanes were laid against it (spec US2 names it). Moves maps: the brook is rounded before the houses see it.
M4_reorders.b_connector_start: stage_track starts the connector at the exit ray's outer end (the ray is fabric-free by reservation) and holds its first bearing within 180 - DOUBLE_BACK_DEG of seat['out'], so ray and connector never fold at their joint.
M4_reorders.c_no_late_lane_writer: stage_crossings no longer rewrites lanes (its square_crossings loop, frame.py:95-103, becomes settle step 1). After stage_web nothing writes a lane: grep-verified today, the only writer outside ways/ is frame.py:103. A unit test walks the stage functions after stage_web and fails on any call of reink_lane/lane/drop_lanes.

rules.rule: No seated farmhouse stands off the connected lane network (every farmhouse within WEB_REACH_FT of the component grown from the connector). Stated: ways/checks.py:unreached_houses; driver.py generate() re-roll; research/contents.json#tiers 'every house in a nucleated cluster is reached'.
rules.owner: l7r/diagram/settlement/rolling/fit.py:_parts_fit (the corridor admitted at seating) + hamletgen/ways/settle.py:settle_the_web step 4 (the corridor drawn). The census named serve.py:_serve_stragglers; the straggler pass cannot own it - 2b shows that by the time it runs no path may exist.
rules.mechanism: M3: each seat is admitted only with a reserved access corridor to the tree rooted at the exit ray; every later placer refuses a footprint on a reserved corridor (s.on_access_corridor); settle step 4 draws, for every house in unreached_houses, its corridor chain to first contact with the served network. Predicate: ways/checks.py:unreached_houses (placer and unit test read it). generate() loses its loop: one build, no avoid list.
rules.fallback: a seat with no admissible corridor is refused and the next seat offered (the seat loop's existing rescue rounds). A household that no seat admits is not seated and is recorded in meta.roll_placed / the seat_search counts - never a stranded house. This can move the seated count; test_every_declared_household_is_seated (homesteads area) holds the 85% floor, and the plan's first measurement is the 48-seed cohort's placed count with the corridor rule on.
rules.later_stages: stage_track (connector starts on the ray: M4b); appurtenances/pond_stock/burial refuse corridors; nothing after stage_web removes lanes (M4c); the corridors are released only after the web has drawn every one it needs.
rules.unit_test: (a) a constructed Settlement with two placed homesteads whose yards and gardens close the only gap to the ray, and a candidate seat behind them: _parts_fit refuses it; a seat with a clear run is admitted and its corridor registered. (b) a byre footprint on a reserved corridor is refused by stage_appurtenances' placer. (c) settle_the_web on constructed lanes that leave one house 200 ft off the network with its corridor reserved: unreached_houses(M) == [] after, and the drawn corridor passes every M1 predicate. (d) generate() builds exactly once (a counter on build) - the loop is gone.
rules.retire: gate/hamletgen/test_driver.py::test_a_map_that_strands_a_farmhouse_is_re_rolled_with_that_ground_forbidden, ::test_a_re_roll_that_does_not_help_is_not_kept, ::test_a_re_roll_resumes_at_the_seats_from_an_untouched_copy, ::test_every_resume_starts_from_the_same_snapshot, ::test_the_stage_profile_takes_the_same_snapshot; hamletgen/test_driver.py::test_a_re_roll_that_seats_fewer_households_is_not_kept, ::test_only_the_attempt_kept_is_finished (the choice it tests is gone; the staging/promote tests stay); settlement/test_rolling.py::test_a_bundle_is_refused_a_seat_the_re_roll_loop_has_already_forbidden; hamletgen/test_site_boundary.py's UnreachableGround test if UnreachableGround is deleted (the corridor test subsumes it - keep it only if measured cheaper as a prefilter); the reach clause of test_a_rolled_cohort_passes_the_whole_gate. Code going with them: driver.resume_at/resume/snapshot/_avoid_seats, homesteads/seats.py:_seat_allowed, the avoid-salted rng in stage_homesteads, Report.attempt/rerolled_after and meta.roll_attempt/roll_after (tooling/ci/test_rollverdict.py's re-roll-attempt cases follow).
rules.risk_why: future-work/farming-communities.md 2b/2b-i records 18 failed attempts on this residue; the reservation reshapes every nucleated cluster (a reserved ray through its middle, corridors between rows) and may lower the seated count - it moves every live pool map.

rules.rule: No lane crosses a brook without a deck whose own span reaches the crossing point. Stated: test_pool_261::test_every_way_across_the_brook_is_bridged; bridges() docstring.
rules.owner: l7r/diagram/settlement/city/bridges.py:BridgesMixin.bridges and BridgesMixin.bridge (census owner right; both dedupes are the gap).
rules.mechanism: one predicate deck_covers(deck, x, y) = dist <= deck['span'] (the test's reading), lifted to bridges.py. bridges() skips a crossing only when an existing deck covers it (not 'within half the NEW span'); bridge()'s _btol early return likewise returns an existing deck only when it covers the point. Where an uncovered crossing's deck would overlap an existing deck on the same water, the existing deck is re-seated to span both crossings (seat_deck on the merged span) instead of skipping.
rules.fallback: none needed after W12: every crossing that reaches bridges() was admitted by deck_seats in settle, and the merge case re-seats; if the merged deck cannot seat, settle step 2 already cut the later lane's crossing (it failed deck_seats against the lanes present), so bridges() never meets it.
rules.later_stages: none: stage_crossings runs after every way (M4c) and nothing lays a lane after it.
rules.unit_test: a constructed map: an oblique brook deck of span 30 at (0,0) and a channel-plank crossing at 12 ft from it along the brook (inside half the new span, outside the plank's own span): bridges() draws a deck covering the second crossing; every crossing of every lane has deck_covers true.
rules.risk_why: a dedupe predicate change; can add a deck on a map where two crossings stood close.

rules.rule: On a brook map some internal lane comes within 60 ft of the paddy or its dry hem - the hamlet has a way to its field. Stated: test_pool_261::test_a_way_reaches_the_field; research/fields/290.
rules.owner: l7r/diagram/hamletgen/ways/bund.py:a_way_onto_the_bund (the census owner is right for the drawing) + the field corridor reserved at seating (settlement/rolling/fit.py:_parts_fit, M3).
rules.mechanism: the tree carries a FIELD edge reserved at seating (M3 field_corridor); a_way_onto_the_bund keeps its joined/run_on/branch order, and its 'none: ...' return is replaced by drawing the reserved field corridor (settle step 7). Predicate law.field_unreached (the test's computation, lifted).
rules.fallback: front-row seats keep being offered until one admits a field corridor; the reserved corridor may cross a ditch (decked) or the brook at a ford, which is what the 'none' branch refused.
rules.later_stages: settle steps never cut tree edges; nothing after stage_web writes lanes.
rules.unit_test: a constructed map whose every straight run from the lanes to the paddy crosses a supply canal (today's 'none' input) with a reserved field corridor: a_way_onto_the_bund + settle leave field_unreached false and the corridor decked at the canal.
rules.risk_why: adds a seating constraint on the front row; the field path moves on maps where it was run_on or branch only if settle had to draw the corridor.

rules.rule: No lane record is an empty husk (< 2 points or < 1 ft). Stated: test_pool_261::test_the_ways_cross_the_brook_only_at_fords_and_never_over_and_back (first clause).
rules.owner: l7r/diagram/hamletgen/ways/settle.py:settle_the_web step 6 (the census named stage_web's closing passes; web.py:667's drop runs before split_at_crossings/tidy/meet_end_to_end, which can each leave one).
rules.mechanism: law.husks; settle drops every husk with s.drop_lanes as its last action of each round.
rules.fallback: drop (a husk draws nothing).
rules.later_stages: none (M4c).
rules.unit_test: lanes with a one-point record and a three-point record at one spot: settle leaves law.husks empty.
rules.retire: the husk assertion of test_the_ways_cross_the_brook_only_at_fords_and_never_over_and_back (the test retires whole when W05-W07 land).
rules.risk_why: drops records that draw nothing.

rules.rule: No lane's end runs on beside another way (a doubled tail at _DOUBLED_DEG). Stated: test_the_ways_cross_the_brook_only_at_fords... (along_tail clause); feature 261.
rules.owner: hamletgen/ways/settle.py step 6, with sweeps.py:_sweep_doubled_tails' cut_at_tail as its repair (the sweep skips spur lanes and never cuts along a narrower lane; the test asks every pair; eight passes run after it).
rules.mechanism: law.doubled_tails asks every ordered pair regardless of width or spur; settle cuts the tail with cut_at_tail (a shortening, so it cannot create another violation but a hook, which the same round removes).
rules.fallback: cut; a lane cut below _WEB_MIN_FT whose house is otherwise unreached is served by its corridor (step 4).
rules.later_stages: none (M4c).
rules.unit_test: a spur lane whose last 30 ft run 2 ft beside a wider lane at 3 deg: settle leaves doubled_tails empty.
rules.risk_why: shortens tails only where the predicate fires; the pool passes it today.

rules.rule: No single lane crosses a brook twice or more (out and back on one link - 'two planks for nothing'). Stated: test_the_ways_cross_the_brook_only_at_fords... (parity clause); sweeps.py:302-304.
rules.owner: hamletgen/ways/sweeps.py:_join_orphan_ways (the fallback) + settle.py step 2 (the guarantee).
rules.mechanism: _join_orphan_ways drops its even-crossing fallback: a link with brook_crossings >= 2 is refused, never kept (FR-005 at the site). law.crossing_faults counts crossings per lane per brook; settle cuts a lane with >= 2 between its first two crossings and keeps the pieces that pass.
rules.fallback: the orphan stays unlinked; settle step 5 drops it and step 4 serves its houses by their corridors (one tree crossing per brook by construction).
rules.later_stages: none (M4c; round_the_brooks moved before the ways, M4a, so a crossing count cannot change after it is judged).
rules.unit_test: (a) _join_orphan_ways on an orphan whose only route crosses a brook out and back: no link drawn. (b) settle on a lane crossing a brook twice: crossing_faults empty after.
rules.retire: with W04; the unit test of the fallback branch in tests/hamletgen/ways/test_sweeps.py, if one exercises the kept out-and-back link.
rules.risk_why: the fallback is rare (Mizuguchi-type maps); refusing it hands those houses to W01.

rules.rule: No lane crosses a brook except at a ford (within FORD_HALF of a recorded ford). Stated: test_the_ways_cross_the_brook_only_at_fords... (ford clause, at 45 ft); track.py:275 fords; checks.py stream_segs.
rules.owner: settle.py step 2; the routers already gap the brook at fords (checks.py:stream_segs) - the leaks are the late rewrites (meet_end_to_end, center_lane_ends, cut_at_tail's snap, a_way_onto_the_bund's run-on) that read no stream_segs, and round_the_brooks moving the course after the fords.
rules.mechanism: M4a puts the rounded course before the fords are computed; law.crossing_faults asks every crossing against meta.brook_fords at FORD_HALF (ONE constant: the test's 45 ft slack is dropped - FR-003); settle cuts an off-ford crossing segment out of a non-tree lane. Corridors cross only at fords (M3).
rules.fallback: cut; stranded houses/field served by corridors.
rules.later_stages: none after M4a/M4c.
rules.unit_test: a lane crossing a brook 60 ft from the nearest ford: settle removes the crossing segment and crossing_faults is empty; a lane crossing inside the ford gap is untouched.
rules.risk_why: M4a rounds the brook before the fords and houses see it - moves every brook map's course, fords and near-brook seats.

rules.rule: No household's way out (its shortest route through the lanes to the connector's outer end) crosses a brook more than once. Stated: test_pool_261::test_every_way_out_crosses_the_brook_at_most_once; settlement-review of Mizuguchi (feature 261).
rules.owner: settle.py step 3 + the tree's one-crossing-per-brook admission (M3). The census named sweeps.py:_link_home_bank, which repairs only where the straggler pass can lay a home-bank way and runs once, before eight more passes.
rules.mechanism: predicate law.way_outs_crossing (departure_routes, as the test). Seat time: the tree crosses each brook at most once and every chain crosses each brook at most once. Settle step 3: while a route crosses twice, drop the non-tree, non-connector lane piece carrying its crossing farthest from the connector. The connector never crosses the brook (connector_track avoids it outright, checks.py:149-152). A shortest route never uses one crossing twice, so once no non-tree crossing lies on a twice-crossing route - finite drops - no route crosses twice; the corridors drawn in step 4 add only the tree crossing, and the loop re-asks step 3 after them. _link_home_bank stays as the best-effort drawing pass it is.
rules.fallback: drop the crossing piece; every house it served that goes unreached is served by its corridor chain (<= 1 crossing by construction).
rules.later_stages: none (M4c).
rules.unit_test: constructed banks A and B, the connector on A, a house on A whose only drawn lanes leave by a plank to B and return by a second plank: settle leaves way_outs_crossing empty and unreached_houses empty (the house's corridor drawn on A).
rules.risk_why: drops real crossing lanes on hamlets astride a brook (Mizuguchi, Kashikawa, Inashiro) and restricts the corridor tree to one crossing per brook, which constrains seats across the water.

rules.rule: No lane ends in a hook: a first or last leg <= _HOOK_FT (12) turning back >= _HOOK_DEG (90). Stated: test_pool_261::test_no_lane_ends_in_a_hook; test_lane_network (hook half); GM 2026-09-26.
rules.owner: settle.py step 2 (joints.py:straighten_joints keeps its repair, but leaves a hook when unhooked/keeps_the_web/commit_lane refuse, and eight writers follow it plus stage_crossings' squaring).
rules.mechanism: law.hooked_ends (every lane, connector included - the stricter of the two tests); settle removes the hook leg (a shortening; repeated until none - a two-point lane cannot hook). For a TREE lane a hook cannot arise: its door end is a single straight leg.
rules.fallback: shorten; a lane shortened away is dropped and its house served by its corridor.
rules.later_stages: stage_crossings' squaring moved into settle step 1, which runs before step 2 in the same loop (M4c).
rules.unit_test: a lane whose last leg is 8 ft at 120 deg: settle leaves hooked_ends empty; a connector with a hook likewise.
rules.retire: test_pool_261.py::test_no_lane_ends_in_a_hook; the hook clause of test_lane_network's joint test (retires with W10).
rules.risk_why: the pool passes it; removes <= 12 ft legs.

rules.rule: Two lanes meeting end to end never double back (turn >= 140 deg at the joint). Stated: gate/test_lane_network.py::test_no_two_lanes_meet_end_to_end_in_a_fold...; GM 2026-09-26.
rules.owner: settle.py step 6; joints.py:straighten_joints/_one_joint stays the best-effort T-maker.
rules.mechanism: law.folded_joints; settle drops the last leg of the shorter record at a folded joint (repeat) - after that the two no longer meet end to end at the fold. Tree edges meet other tree edges at a T (foot on a segment interior), and a corridor whose foot is a segment END is admitted at seating only if the joint turn < 140.
rules.fallback: shorten/drop; houses served by corridors.
rules.later_stages: split_at_crossings creates new joints - it runs before settle; nothing after.
rules.unit_test: two records meeting end to end at 160 deg: settle leaves folded_joints empty and unreached_houses unchanged.
rules.risk_why: repairs a shape the pool does not ship.

rules.rule: Every lane crosses the brook and every drawn channel within FORD_SQUARE_TOL_DEG (10) of square. Stated: test_pool_261::test_every_lane_crosses_a_drawn_channel_square and ::test_every_lane_crosses_the_brook_square; research 0084.
rules.owner: hamletgen/ways/checks.py:square_crossings, called from settle step 1 (moved out of frame.py:stage_crossings). The census owner is right about the function; the call site moves.
rules.mechanism: square_crossings repaired to be total: split a segment too short to hold the square leg at the crossing (instead of 'left as drawn'), square every crossing on a segment (not break after the first), and iterate streams and drawn channels together until a pass changes nothing (so squaring at the head race cannot leave the brook crossing oblique). law.crossing_faults' squareness clause is the test's computation. Where the square leg would make the lane bend badly (the 2*half leg is two turns within ~16 ft), settle step 2 cuts the crossing out rather than keep a kink; corridors are admitted at seating already squared and bend-legal.
rules.fallback: cut the crossing segment from a non-tree lane; the corridor serves.
rules.later_stages: stage_crossings stops rewriting lanes (M4c); round_the_brooks is before the ways (M4a), so the course squared against is the course drawn.
rules.unit_test: a lane crossing a brook at 40 deg on a 6 ft segment (today's 'left as drawn' case) and a lane crossing a head race and the brook 10 ft apart: after settle, every crossing within 10 deg and no bends_badly.
rules.risk_why: moves every crossing's geometry on brook maps (and the squaring now runs before the woods instead of after them).

rules.rule: Every drawn deck spans its water: no corner in the water, a landing on dry ground each side (a way crosses water square enough to be decked). Stated: gate/test_crossings_and_cover.py::test_every_deck_is_long_enough_to_land_on_dry_ground (bridges_span_their_water); seat_deck docstring; future-work 2f and 'the oblique-deck growth loop fails SILENTLY'.
rows: R3 future-work 'the oblique-deck growth loop fails SILENTLY'
R3 future-work 2f 'The shallow-crossing veto must be STREAM-scoped' (seed 47, 17 deg link)
rules.owner: settle.py step 2 (law.deck_seats) decides which crossings exist; bridges.py:bridges draws. The census named bridges() alone - it runs after every way is final and can only draw or not.
rules.mechanism: ONE predicate: seat_deck(...)[2] with _deck_corners_clear (the placer's corner test, stronger than the test's 'span >= water width'; the test is rewritten to call it - FR-003). Settle admits a crossing only if seat_deck seats a deck there against bridge_crossed_waters(M) (the same list bridges() reads). Step 1 squares brook/channel crossings first, so the 17 deg link of seed 47 becomes square before it is judged. bridges() then draws only seated decks; seat_deck's 'return the undersized span' branch becomes unreachable and is replaced by raising (a bug, not a map).
rules.fallback: an unseatable crossing is cut from the non-tree lane; corridors are admitted at seating only with deck_seats true.
rules.later_stages: none (bridges() reads exactly the lanes settle left; M4a gives it the same course).
rules.unit_test: (a) seat_deck on a near-parallel crossing returns seated False; (b) settle on a lane with that crossing removes it; (c) bridges() on settled lanes: every deck _deck_corners_clear; (d) a lane crossing at 17 deg is squared and decked.
rules.retire: gate/test_crossings_and_cover.py::test_every_deck_is_long_enough_to_land_on_dry_ground; any unit test asserting seat_deck's undersized return is drawn.
rules.risk_why: can cut crossings on maps with oblique field-ditch crossings (not squared by W11's scope), handing their houses to corridors.

rules.rule: A carried deck lands on dry ground, never on a flooded field (the deck's landing may not run onto the paddy). Stated: R3 'The field path's canal deck runs onto the paddy' (LANDING_FT 10 ft puts the end 7 ft onto the paddy); roads_bridge_water.
rows: R3 same section, 'The field path's canal deck runs onto the paddy'
rules.owner: settlement/city/bridges.py:seat_deck / _deck_corners_clear (the deck search) - the census owner (bridges() + the field path's crossing form) is right.
rules.mechanism: extend the deck predicate: a corner is legal only if clear of the water AND outside every flooded field polygon (crop_polys); for a crossing whose way ends on the bund within LANDING_FT of the water (the run-on's over_the_water end, OVER_THE_WATER_FT 3.5), the deck takes the channel-footbridge form (plank_w, PLANK_ABUTMENT) - the R3 sketch - sized by the same seat_deck. law.deck_seats uses the extended predicate, so settle refuses a crossing whose deck cannot land dry.
rules.fallback: the footbridge form; if even that lands wet, settle cuts the crossing and the field corridor (W03) serves.
rules.later_stages: none.
rules.unit_test: a field path ending 3.5 ft past a 4.5 ft canal on the bund: the deck drawn has no corner inside the paddy polygon.
rules.retire: none (no finished-map test asserts it today; this adds the unit test the R3 row owes).
rules.risk_why: still_open unknown; changes the deck form on field paths over canals.

rules.rule: A footplank is laid on a recorded supply ditch (main or branch), never off a ditch and never on the collector, drain or feeder. Stated: gate/test_crossings_and_cover.py::test_every_plank_crosses_a_supply_ditch_and_never_the_collector.
rules.owner: settlement/city/bridges.py:channel_footbridges (census owner right).
rules.mechanism: ONE predicate plank_on_supply(pt, field_ditches) = the nearest recorded ditch to the plank's center is within 24 ft and has role main or branch (the test's computation, lifted); channel_footbridges skips a ditch whose role is not main/branch for every archetype (not only through the polder's seg_caps) and refuses a seat where plank_on_supply is false (the main/drain junction case).
rules.fallback: the ditch carries no plank; no rule demands one per ditch (long_ditches_have_a_footbridge is retired - only its name survives in tests/fixtures/gate_check_names.json).
rules.later_stages: none.
rules.unit_test: a comb field with a 996 px drain and a main meeting it: no plank on the drain; a plank seated at the junction whose nearest ditch is the drain is refused.
rules.risk_why: removes planks from drains; the reference roll has none there today.

rules.rule: A plank stands only on water that earns one (worth_planking at the seat's own taper). Stated: waterfields/frame.py:worth_planking; bridges.py:377-386 comment.
rules.owner: settlement/city/bridges.py:channel_footbridges.
rules.mechanism: _wide_enough becomes a hard filter on the candidate seats (drop the sort-that-keeps-narrow-last). The reason it was a preference - the gate demanding one plank per long ditch - is retired (no live test demands it), so the placer/check split it prevented no longer exists.
rules.fallback: no plank on that slot/ditch.
rules.later_stages: none.
rules.unit_test: a tapering branch whose qualifying run is fully blocked by a house: no plank is laid on its narrow part.
rules.risk_why: affects a rare branch (cohort seeds 41, 43 before the preference).

rules.rule: No internal lane end stops in open ground: each end reaches another way (not merely the one its own far end stands on), a farmhouse, the bund, or a steading it has arrived at. Stated: gate/test_lane_network.py::test_every_lane_end_reaches_something_worth_walking_to and ::test_every_shipped_hamlets_lane_ends_reach_something; test_pool_261::test_no_lane_end_is_served_only_by_the_way_it_left; geom.end_serves.
rules.owner: settle.py step 6. The census split it across sweeps.py:_sweep_dangling_ends (restores the dangling original when a pull-back strands a house) and web.py:tidy_lane_ends (trims against every other lane, the one it left included); both run before end-moving passes.
rules.mechanism: law.dangling_ends = end_serves over the stronger segment set (other lanes minus those within _TOUCH_GAP of the lane's own far end) - one predicate for all three tests (FR-003: tidy and the tests read different sets today). Settle trims each failing non-tree end with _trim_to_service at that predicate; where the trim would strand a house (the 'keep' case that today leaves the lane whole or restores it), the lane is trimmed anyway and the house is served by its corridor - the keep exemption goes. Tree edges serve at both ends by construction (door; a T on a drawn lane).
rules.fallback: trim or drop; never restore the dangling original (sweeps.py's restore + carry_to_dooryard-None branch becomes a trim).
rules.later_stages: meet_end_to_end and a_way_onto_the_bund run before settle; nothing after.
rules.unit_test: (a) a lane that leaves the connector and stops 61 ft past its house (Mizuguchi): after settle its end serves; (b) a lane that is a house's only way and dangles: trimmed, the house's corridor drawn, unreached_houses empty.
rules.retire: gate/test_lane_network.py::test_every_lane_end_reaches_something_worth_walking_to, ::test_every_shipped_hamlets_lane_ends_reach_something; test_pool_261.py::test_no_lane_end_is_served_only_by_the_way_it_left; the restore-branch unit test in tests/hamletgen/ways/test_sweeps.py if it asserts the restore.
rules.risk_why: the stronger predicate trims lanes the pool now ships as passing tidy's weaker reading; the trim-lane-stubs record (43/48 -> 9/48) warns that a blanket trim eats joins - here tree edges are exempt and joins end ON a way, so they serve.

rules.rule: The lanes form ONE network at the 4 ft ink tolerance (every lane end within _TOUCH_GAP of the rest). Stated: gate/test_lane_network.py::test_every_lane_belongs_to_one_network and ::test_every_shipped_hamlets_lanes_are_one_network_at_the_ink_tolerance; fabric.py:275-281.
rules.owner: settle.py step 5 (census: stage_web; right in spirit, but no pass there holds it after the last join).
rules.mechanism: law.networks = _components(ways, _TOUCH_GAP) (both tests' reading). Settle drops every component not containing the connector; the houses it served that go unreached get their corridor chains (step 4), which join the connector's component through the root. _draw_web's refused join (a link through a farmhouse) stays refused - that refusal is right; the orphan it leaves is now dropped rather than shipped.
rules.fallback: drop the orphan component; corridors serve its houses.
rules.later_stages: stage_crossings no longer rewrites lanes (M4c) - the census's named risk.
rules.unit_test: a web with a piece 30 ft from the rest whose only link would touch a farmhouse corner: after settle, networks == 1 and unreached_houses empty.
rules.risk_why: dropping orphan pieces can remove visible lanes on maps whose join is refused (Sawada, Kashikawa 2026-08-29 cases).

rules.rule: A lane bends like a path: no turn >= 140 deg, no two turns >= 50 deg within 40 ft of path (non-connector lanes). Stated: gate/test_lane_network.py::test_no_lane_doubles_back_or_kinks; gate/test_cohort_lane_rules.py; soak polder and seed-43 tests; research/questions/0081-village-lanes.html.
rules.owner: settle.py step 2 + serve.py:_serve_stragglers (the fallback). The census named serve.py; the web's later rewrites (may_write is 'no worse', not 'good') also emit it.
rules.mechanism: ONE predicate law.bends_badly = the tests' _kinks run-sum (clearance._bends_badly, which tests two turns separated by ONE segment, is replaced everywhere it is read - may_write, serve's ranking - FR-003). serve.py stops drawing the least-bad fold (_folded is deleted: a folded path is refused like a steading foul). Settle cuts a non-tree lane at the offending turn and keeps the longer legal side. Seed 43's lattice step round a house corner is two 50-deg turns within 40 ft: the settle cut removes it, and the house it served is reached by its corridor (straight by construction).
rules.fallback: refuse the fold (serve), cut the kink (settle); the corridor serves.
rules.later_stages: squaring is settle step 1, judged by step 2 in the same round (the census's named risk: a square leg is a kink when the lane met the brook > 50 deg off square).
rules.unit_test: (a) serve on a constructed pocket where every door path folds: no path drawn (and the corridor drawn by settle); (b) settle on seed 43's recorded geometry (specs/215-the-floor-itself/census/kink-seed-43.json) as a constructed lane: bends_badly false after; (c) a three-short-leg zigzag the old _bends_badly passed and the rule fails: bends_badly true.
rules.retire: gate/test_lane_network.py::test_no_lane_doubles_back_or_kinks; gate/test_cohort_lane_rules.py (whole module, and the COHORT rolls it alone required - check tests/rolls.py roster rows); soak/test_seed_43_kink.py (whole module); soak/test_polder_fall_0.py::test_the_polder_s_lanes_bend_like_paths; any unit test of serve.py's folded last resort.
rules.risk_why: seed 43 has resisted the router for three features (166 R2b, 215, 216); cutting kinks moves lanes on every map where the old one-segment predicate let a spread kink through.

rules.rule: No lane's tread runs through a steading's fabric: a house, farm shed or byre (and a neighbor's yard or garden) - a door path is exempt only from its own steading. Stated: gate/test_lane_network.py::test_a_lane_does_not_break_mid_run; serve.py:550-555 (the overlap matrix; cohort seed 18).
rules.owner: settle.py step 2 + serve.py (the ranking fallback). Census owner stage_web.
rules.mechanism: law.fouls_fabric (fabric._hits_a_steading + _crosses_fabric against passable at _TOUCH_GAP). serve.py's cut ranking skips a fouling cut (continue) instead of ranking it - FR-005 at the site. Settle cuts a fouling segment out of a non-tree lane (the census's risk: square_crossings rewrote lanes with no footprint test - it is now judged in the same round). The test's 'segment > 60 px whose midpoint is in a solid bbox' is implied by the stronger predicate and the test is replaced by its unit test.
rules.fallback: cut; corridor serves.
rules.later_stages: none (M4c).
rules.unit_test: a straggler cut grazing a neighbor's garden at 1.2 ft (seed 18) and a lane leg across a byre: no drawn lane fouls_fabric after serve + settle.
rules.risk_why: a cut through a squared crossing near a steading can remove a lane a map relies on; the corridor replaces it.

rules.rule: No farmhouse is the terminus of more than two free lane ends within 80 ft. Stated: gate/test_lane_network.py::test_a_farmhouse_discharges_one_lane_end_not_three (lane_ends_front_different_houses); consts.py 0611 ruling.
rules.owner: settle.py step 6 (census: serve.py:_serve_stragglers - no engine code counts ends per house today, grep-confirmed by the census).
rules.mechanism: law.doorstep_ends (the test's count, lifted). Settle trims the extra non-tree ends back to a T on the nearest lane within reach, else back to where they stop serving only that house and are then trimmed by the end rule; a corridor contributes one end (its door end).
rules.fallback: trim/drop the extra ends; the house keeps its corridor or one lane.
rules.later_stages: none.
rules.unit_test: three lanes ending 30-60 ft from one house: after settle, doorstep_ends empty and the house reached.
rules.risk_why: a new repair with no prior engine code; trims visible lanes at busy dooryards.

rules.rule: A join meets its way as a T, never a needle (a last leg running back along the tread it meets at a shallow angle). Stated: R3 'A needle join' (Mizuguchi, 35 ft at 16 deg, ~250 sq ft needle); web.py:660-666 records a squared-join fix tried and reverted at the 269 landing.
rules.owner: settle.py step 6 (census: web.py join + tidy).
rules.mechanism: law.needle_joins (NEW predicate, thresholds a map drawing convention to record). Settle cuts the needle leg back to its prior vertex and ends it square on the tread (the foot of that vertex) - the reverted attempt's move - and, the part that attempt lacked, the tidy no longer trims the tread's tail that served a gable-end house because that house is re-checked by unreached_houses and served by its corridor if the trim strands it; the entrance-board route clause (test_an_entrance_board_stands_at_the_entrance, notices area) reads departure_routes after settle.
rules.fallback: cut to the prior vertex; drop if it no longer serves.
rules.later_stages: stage_notice seats the board after settle, so it sees the final routes.
rules.unit_test: Mizuguchi's recorded join as constructed lanes: needle_joins empty after settle, unreached_houses empty, networks == 1.
rules.risk_why: the same fix was reverted at the 269 landing for costing an entrance board's route; recorded in web.py and future-work.

rules.rule: A lane and the connector never double back side by side over a short leg (hairpin_over_a_short_leg). Stated: R3 'A lane and the connector doubling back' (Kuwabata: 126 ft at 169 deg, 15-40 ft apart); lanes_bend_like_paths.
rows: R3 same section, 'A lane and the connector doubling back' (Kuwabata)
rules.owner: joints.py:fold_the_connector_hairpin (census right) - refused today by may_write; guaranteed by settle step 6.
rules.mechanism: law.connector_hairpins; M4b starts the connector on the exit ray, so a lane arriving at its start meets the ray's lane end to end or as a T; settle drops the lane's short last leg (fold_the_connector_hairpin's own edit, without moving the connector) whenever the hairpin is present - removing the leg cannot be refused, and a lane shortened away hands its houses to corridors.
rules.fallback: drop the leg.
rules.later_stages: none.
rules.unit_test: Kuwabata's recorded geometry: connector_hairpins empty after settle.
rules.risk_why: still_open unknown; the connector's start moves with M4b on every map.

rules.rule: The connector never runs through marsh/wet ground or across a steading (roads_clear_of_marsh, houses_off_corridors). Stated: track.py:614-636 (GM: 'a path does not pass through marshland'); checks.py:149-152.
rules.owner: hamletgen/ways/track.py:connector_track (census right).
rules.mechanism: accept only soaked == 0 and steaded == 0 (crop hits stay repairable by W24). Steadings cannot foul a bearing that starts at the exit ray's outer end and leaves within 180 - 140 deg of seat['out'] (M4b), because the ray is reserved and every house stands inside out_reach. For wet ground, when no bearing of the sweep is dry, a DRY-EXIT path: one flood fill over a coarse grid (20 ft) of the ground known at stage_track (wet grown by 8 px, envelope, crop, pond, brook except at fords), BFS from the start to the frame edge, string-pulled against the same PathChecker - the one design 2b records the router cannot express (it caps at 90,000 cells), and cheap here because it runs at most once per map.
rules.fallback: the dry-exit path. Its existence is a seat-time property of the cluster anchor (seat_cluster must refuse an anchor from which no dry exit reaches the frame - the SEATING area's rule; raised here as a cross-area dependency).
rules.later_stages: _pull_back_to_service shortens the connector only along its own track; settle never cuts the connector.
rules.unit_test: a start pocketed by a toe marsh spanning the canvas except one dry neck: connector_track returns a path with zero wet violations through the neck; a start with steadings on every bearing but the reserved ray: steaded == 0.
rules.retire: any unit test in tests/hamletgen/ways/test_track.py that asserts the least-bad bearing is returned.
rules.risk_why: the connector's start moves on every map (M4b); the dry-exit path is new code on a rare branch.

rules.rule: A track meeting a field goes round it: no connector leg crosses a crop outline (fields_clear_of_road, lanes_clear_of_dry_plots; GM Inashiro 2026-08-12). Stated: clearance.py:route_around docstring.
rules.owner: hamletgen/ways/clearance.py:route_around, called by track.py:stage_track.
rules.mechanism: iterate until no leg crosses ANY crop polygon (not six rounds of one), bounded by the total ring vertex count (each splice consumes ring edges), then verify with the stage's PathChecker; if a crossing survives, return None and connector_track takes its next clean bearing, then the dry-exit path (W23), which is planned with crop as a wall.
rules.fallback: the next bearing / the dry-exit path; never a crossing path.
rules.later_stages: _thread_the_fabric clips the result against fabric only (W25).
rules.unit_test: a deeply lobed outline needing seven splices: route_around returns a path clear of it; an unsplicable case returns None.
rules.risk_why: rare branch; the loop bound is a proof, not a tuning.

rules.rule: No track (connector or field spur) is drawn across a steading. Stated: track.py:194 ('THE FALLBACK MUST NOT BE THE OFFENDING RUN'); no_farmhouse_stands_on_a_lane, houses_clear_of_lanes; future-work 'the field SPUR can be forced onto a house' (tripwire seed 27).
rows: R3 future-work 'OPEN 2026-08-24: the field SPUR can be forced onto a house'
rules.owner: hamletgen/ways/track.py:_thread_the_fabric and stage_track's spur_path (census right).
rules.mechanism: _thread_the_fabric never returns a run for which _crosses_fabric(run, fabric, gap) is true: its terminal returns [] instead of `out`/`run`. For the connector this terminal is unreachable after M4b (the start is on the reserved ray and W23 admits only steaded == 0) and raises; for the spur, spur targets are ranked by a fabric-clear route and an empty result is a recorded drop (meta spur shortfall, already written), the field reached by W03.
rules.fallback: spur: drop, recorded; field way by the field corridor. Connector: cannot occur (raise).
rules.later_stages: none.
rules.unit_test: a spur whose run[0] stands inside a neighbor's yard with no clear route: _thread_the_fabric returns [] and stage_track records the spur dropped; no lane crosses a footprint.
rules.retire: the 'pragma: no cover' swing-ladder note stays with its branch; any unit test asserting the original run is returned.
rules.risk_why: the spur is dropped only on tight clusters; W03 guarantees the field regardless.

cross_area_dependencies: SEATING (homesteads/cluster owner): M3 adds a refusal to _parts_fit and a footprint test to every later part placer (s.on_access_corridor); the household floor (test_every_declared_household_is_seated, 85%) must be re-measured with it - the first measurement of the plan: the 48-seed cohort's roll_placed and seat_search with the corridor rule on, against today. W23's dry exit makes 'a dry way from the anchor to the frame' a seat_cluster refusal.

WATER (sink/frame owner): M4a moves round_the_brooks after stage_sink and writes the rounded course to plan.brook/plan.sink_brook; any rule on the brook's shape (test_no_brook_segment_lies_on_a_screen_axis_but_the_tap_run, the ruled-along-the-frame test) must be guaranteed on the rounded course, which is now final before the houses.
NOTICES/ENTRANCE (siting owner): W08/W16/W17/W21 can drop lanes, so the entrance board's route test reads the settled web - stage_notice already runs after it.

WOODS (woodland/copse owner): the reserved corridors are released after stage_web, so no vegetation rule changes; stage_crossings no longer rewrites lanes after the woods (M4c), which removes the census's 'rewrite after the woods' risk for them too.
measurements_owed_before_building: the 48-seed cohort + pool with M3 alone: roll_placed per seed, seat_search candidates/refusals, unreached_houses before settle (should be [] wherever corridors are drawn) - scored with unreached_houses itself, never a hand-rolled reach measure (2b's broken-instrument lesson).
settle_the_web rounds and seconds per pool map (the perf bookend, SC-006).
how many lanes settle cuts per map on the current pool (expected ~0: every pool map passes the finished-map tests today) - a nonzero count on a pool map is a finding to record, not noise.
